audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer reads Yasuo/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yasuo while the content layer and the packet both read Katarina/Yasuo/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Yasuo/Katarina. Every row disagrees across the two layers.
audit.why: The content whys are grounded — level 1 Steel Tempest is a single 475 line with no E loop yet, level 2 his 0.5s Sweeping Blade weaving plus the Way of the Wanderer shield wins short trades, and first item is his crit spike. The full layer is undifferentiated template text.
audit.corrected: All seven full-layer sides moved to the content values with ratings and whys rewritten to match.

audit.why: spikes[] correctly place the 3-5 window as yours, the first-item crit curve as his, and late as yours off flanks. Last Breath at 70/50/30s requires an Airborne target he can only self-generate with the two-stack Steel Tempest tornado.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction is stated only vaguely: Wind Wall blocks projectiles, and Katarina's Q Dagger throw IS a projectile while Shunpo is a targeted blink that is not. The page says 'bypasses Wind Wall' without ever saying why. It also never states that Wind Wall has a facing and blocks from one side only.
audit.why: ownerKit Q carries the projectile flag; ownerKit E is a blink to target with no projectile flag. enemyKit W carries blocksProjectiles and terrain and lasts 4 seconds.
audit.corrected: Stated explicitly in breakdown.cooldowns and the Do's bullets: the Dagger is blocked, the blink is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second' Wind Wall window.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and 17s at rank 5 with a 4-second duration. Fifteen appears nowhere in his kit. Sweeping Blade is effectively free at 0.5s down to 0.1s, which is the real reason he is hard to pin.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d is tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d is tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); both sit under titles about W spacing and spent Shunpo charges. tradeBad itself references 'CC still loaded' when Yasuo's only CC is a knock-up he has to build stacks for.
audit.why: Titles promise one thing and the bodies explain another, and the pasted line describes a held stun that does not exist in this kit.
audit.corrected: Both bullets rewritten to their titles and to Yasuo's actual pattern.

edits.before: Q the wave and collect the dagger — every pickup is a free spin; the lane learns your dagger geometry or bleeds.
edits.after: One rank of Steel Tempest is a 475 line and nothing else — your Q-auto trade beats him before Sweeping Blade gives him a harass loop.

edits.before: W joins: drop, dance, collect — the self-dagger speeds your trades and your exits both.
edits.after: His level 2 is the flip: E through a minion into Q, with the moving shield already built. Give him this window and keep your bar above 70%.

edits.before: Full kit: E to daggers, not faces — the blink economy is the champion; trade only through steel on the ground.
edits.after: Shunpo is a blink, not a projectile — land behind him and Wind Wall is facing the wrong way while your full string lands.

edits.before: Dagger-trade on cooldown: Q-E-W-E strings chunk and the resets... wait for kills. Bank the patterns.
edits.after: Chunk-and-leave beats his pre-item sustain as long as you dodge the two-stack tornado. Fight off the wave where his E has nothing to hop.

edits.before: Death Lotus online — any 2v2 near your daggers is a blender invoice. The reset engine is armed.
edits.after: Your 6 needs only his back turned; his needs an Airborne target he can only make himself. Do not eat the tornado and Last Breath stays dead.

edits.before: First item spike: full dagger strings delete squishies and one kill opens the chain reaction.
edits.after: His crit curve arrives first and Wind Wall now eats your thrown steel in a long fight. Shove and take his bot lane, not his health bar.

edits.before: Late Kata is a chain reaction: enter on daggers, lotus the clump, reset through the wreckage, repeat until silence.
edits.after: In a fight he is either diving your carry or walling for his own — both turn his back. Enter from fog and reset through his squishy line.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It governs your forward steps. - E Shunpo (second use) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed, and stands for 4 seconds — it eats your thrown Dagger but never your Shunpo. - Sweeping Blade is 0.5s and drops to 0.1s: off the wave he has no targets, so fight where minions are not. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and needs an Airborne target he has to build himself.

edits.before: Keep W speed as the spacing tool
edits.after: Enter with the blink, not the throw

edits.before: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow.
edits.after: The Dagger is a projectile and the wall deletes it; Shunpo is a targeted blink and passes straight through. Lead with E, throw once you are past.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Yasuo spends Wind Wall on a wave or a whiff — that is 25 seconds at rank 1 with nothing in front of him.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: His only interrupt is the two-stack tornado. Count his Steel Tempest casts and spin after it is spent, not into a loaded one.

edits.before: Your lotus dies to one interrupt — counting their CC before spinning is the entire skill floor of the champion.
edits.after: On a stacked wave his 0.1s E gives him infinite repositioning and his shield rebuilds every step. Melee brawls on a big wave are his format.

edits.before: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.
edits.after: With both blinks gone you cannot get behind him and cannot leave — you are standing in front of a wall he keeps pointed at you.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your thrown steel, weaving E through the wave to reset spacing, and hitting his crit spike before you convert.

edits.before: Ahead, chain it: zone Yasuo off daggers, lotus every skirmish, and reset through the map — fed Katarina is a weather event.
edits.after: Ahead, take the wave off him: no minions means no Sweeping Blade targets and no crit gold. Shove, roam, and make him farm from behind.

edits.before: Carry through chain reactions — one kill is three; your job is the first domino and the discipline to wait for it.
edits.after: Carry from behind him. Wind Wall has a front and Last Breath needs a knock-up; deny both by choosing the angle and the fight never includes his kit.

edits.before: If Yasuo gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Wind Wall extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q bounces and stay relevant through reset potential.
edits.after: A fed Yasuo reaches his crit spike early and the stat-check arrives ahead of schedule. Farm from max Q range, never contest the wave he is standing on, and let your jungler come from the side his wall is not facing.

edits.before: You are the cleanup that starts fights: enter on steel, lotus the clump, reset through the kill, and exit through the panic.
edits.after: You enter second. He commits with Last Breath or spends the wall on his own carry, and the moment either happens his back is open for the spin.

edits.before: Level 1 you win: Steel Tempest is a fixed thin line and your Q-auto trade beats his single-dash pattern before he has E ranks to weave. Poke him off CS. Level 2 flips briefly — Q plus E gives him minion-hopping harass and a shield (Way of the Wanderer) that eats your Bouncing Blade for free, and his early trade DPS is real. Give him the level 2 window, keep your health above 70%, and don't wrestle his shield-cycled short trades.
edits.after: Level 1 you win: Steel Tempest is a fixed 475 line and your Q-auto trade beats his single-dash pattern before he has E ranks to weave. Poke him off CS. Level 2 flips briefly — Q plus a 0.5-second E gives him minion-hopping harass, and the Way of the Wanderer shield builds while he moves and eats your Dagger for free. Give him the level 2 window, keep your health above 70%, and don't wrestle his shield-cycled short trades.

edits.before: Wall your Bouncing Blade and Dagger drops, then E-Q through minions onto you
edits.after: Wall your thrown Dagger, then weave E-Q through minions onto you

notes: Every level-chart row disagreed between layers: full read Yasuo/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yasuo, content and packet read Katarina/Yasuo/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Yasuo/Katarina. All seven full-layer sides moved to the content values as one atomic group, each with its why rewritten; no content win[N] edits were needed because that layer already held the correct verdicts. Corrected the invented 'fifteen-second' Wind Wall figure — it is 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed. Removed 'Bouncing Blade' as a name for Katarina's Q: Riot's text in the kit file gives that slot no ability name, so I described the thrown Dagger instead of asserting one. IMPORTANT for the QA pass: Katarina's Q in the kit carries a derived 'grounding — shuts off enemy dashes' flag, but Riot's own description for that ability says nothing about grounding. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and did NOT write any advice about her Q denying Sweeping Blade or Last Breath. If that flag is real it would be the single strongest line in this matchup and worth a targeted check. Also unverified and left alone: whether Wind Wall blocks a Dagger already lying on the ground being picked up, and the specific first-item names in spikes[2] (Berserker's, Blade of the Ruined King, Statikk) — item builds are not in the kit data. | COHERENCE: 2 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
